factProposals.value: The Next.js frontend does not write to Supabase-backed operator data directly for uploads -- it invokes the existing Python pipeline (pipeline/export_normalizer.py) as a subprocess from a server-side API route, and the DATABASE_URL credential that pipeline needs is read only by that Python process from the repo-root .env, never entering the Node process's environment or the browser bundle.

The frontend's only Supabase credential is NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY, and export_conversions/hospital_monthly_metrics (STORY-011) have RLS enabled with zero policies on purpose -- the anon key cannot read or write either table. Any future frontend feature needing to query these tables directly (not just trigger the Python pipeline) will need either a service-role credential used only server-side, or RLS policies from STORY-006.
factProposals.evidence: frontend/.env.local (NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY only); pipeline/schema.sql (RLS blocks with no policies)

factProposals.value: The upload API route returns a real per-outcome HTTP status (200 accepted, 409 duplicate, 422 needs_mapping/phi_rejected/failed, 400 malformed request, 500 unexpected), verified live via curl against the running dev server, not a mocked handler.

The Python subprocess's stdout can contain more than one JSON line -- the PHI gate's structured audit log line is printed before the CLI's own --json result line -- so a consumer must parse the last line of stdout, not assume it is a single line.
factProposals.evidence: frontend/src/lib/exportUpload.ts#parseNormalizerOutput; frontend/src/lib/exportUpload.test.ts#'uses the last line when the PHI audit log line precedes the result'

decisions.statement: Built the upload feature as a subprocess bridge to the existing pipeline/export_normalizer.py rather than following the story's own suggested approach of writing via supabase-js from Next.js.
decisions.rationale: The suggested approach could not actually work: the frontend's anon key cannot read or write export_conversions/hospital_monthly_metrics, which have RLS enabled with zero policies by STORY-011's own design. Reusing the already-built, already-tested Python normalizer avoided reimplementing hash-dedup, format detection, and the PHI gate a second time in TypeScript, and needed no new credential. Raised with the user, who deferred to best judgment on the architecture.
decisions.evidence: frontend/src/app/api/upload/route.ts module docstring; PROGRESS.md STORY-005 entry

decisions.statement: Added is_duplicate to ConversionOutcome and a --json CLI mode to pipeline/export_normalizer.py, extending a previously-shipped file rather than only writing new frontend code.
decisions.rationale: STORY-011 only needed re-running the same file to leave the correct end state, never needed to report 'this was a repeat' as a distinct outcome. STORY-005's acceptance criteria explicitly require a duplicate message, and the Node bridge needs a stable, parseable contract rather than string-sniffing human-readable CLI text.

decisions.statement: Returned a JSON API response with real per-outcome HTTP status codes rather than a redirect-based, JS-free form flow (the pattern STORY-003's search page uses).
decisions.rationale: A JSON contract is directly verifiable with curl without following a redirect and scraping rendered HTML, and is the more idiomatic pattern for a file-upload interaction than a full-page form submission.

decisions.statement: Did not implement Supabase Storage for the raw uploaded file.
decisions.rationale: STORY-005's acceptance criteria test accept/process, duplicate rejection, and hash-based dedup -- not later file retrievability. Adding a storage bucket now would add integration surface (bucket policies, another credential) not required by anything currently being tested.

decisions.statement: Installed @playwright/test and Chromium as a frontend dev dependency to get real browser automation, rather than requesting a new MCP tool, after the user asked how to obtain it once the initial curl-only verification was flagged as a partial substitute.
decisions.rationale: Playwright is already this project's stated standard for browser E2E work, and it needs no special tool integration -- it runs like any other test command. This closes the earlier browser-automation gap rather than leaving it open.

limitations.statement: The subprocess bridge assumes the Node process and the Python venv share a filesystem and a working directory relationship (frontend/ one level below the repo root) -- this works for local development but has not been evaluated against a serverless deployment target (e.g. Vercel), where a Python venv is not available to a Node function the same way.

demonstrationEvidence.ref: pipeline/test_export_normalizer.py (+2 tests); frontend/src/lib/exportUpload.test.ts (12 tests: every normalizer status parsed correctly, duplicate taking priority over the underlying status, the HTTP status mapping for every outcome, and the multi-line-stdout parsing bug found live); full pipeline/ suite (90 tests) and frontend vitest suite (24 tests) run clean, tsc and eslint clean

frontend/e2e/upload.spec.ts (3 real headless-Chromium tests against the actual running app: valid export accepted, identical re-upload shows duplicate, PHI-bearing export rejected); run twice back to back to confirm the suite is genuinely re-runnable, and DB rows confirmed empty by direct query after each run
